# =============================================================================
# Billable Hours — 2 · the opening (sheets/OPENING.md), a staged open
# boot (her room, 07:00) → breakfast (the family, the start choice) → the firm
# (Callahan, the shift, Theo) → dinner (Jade's text, how this works) → play.
# Clock: 07:00 → exit +10 → 07:10 · two default exits +6 → 07:16 · +165 → ~10:01 at
# the firm · +50 → ~11:00 · +390 → ~17:24 · +45 → ~18:09 at dinner (gates.py _funnel_walk measured 17:54 with +30, before dinner's 18:00 window) · handover ~18:22.
# =============================================================================

# ── screen 1 · the boot ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
[[canvases]]
id   = "opening_boot"
name = "Monday"
description = "Boot. Who she is, the bill, what she wants. Sets opening_boot."

[canvases.trigger]
location      = "her_room"
is_repeatable = false
priority      = 12
is_active     = true

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "wake"
name = "Monday, seven o'clock"
blocks = [
  { type = "image", props = { file = "scenes/opening_her_room.jpg", description = "A young woman sitting up in a narrow bed, morning light, a work blouse on a hanger", search_queries = ["young woman waking small bedroom morning light", "work blouse hanging bedroom door"] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "It's seven o'clock on Monday, and today you start at Callahan Reed. You're Emma, you're twenty-one, and you've been out of college for exactly one summer." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "Here's the problem. Your stepfather Martin paid off your credit card in June, all of it, in one phone call. Now you pay him back: $250 every Friday to start, out of a $350 week. He's already told you the number goes up. He's a partner at the firm. He got you the job. You live in his house." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "And here's what you want. You want to be kept on at the end of the twelve weeks, and you want everyone in that building to stop thinking of you as Martin's favour." },
  { type = "thought_bubble", props = { speaker = "player" }, content = "Twelve weeks. I can do anything for twelve weeks." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "location"
text = "Get dressed and go down."

[canvases.nodes.exit_block.config]
destinationType          = "specific"
locationId               = "kitchen"
time_progression_minutes = 10
flagEffects = [ { targetType = "player", flag = "opening_boot", op = "set" } ]
wardrobeEffects = [
  { action = "equip", item_id = "blouse_white" },
  { action = "equip", item_id = "skirt_pencil" },
  { action = "equip", item_id = "heels_black" },
  { action = "equip", item_id = "bra_plain" },
  { action = "equip", item_id = "panties_plain" },
]

# ── screens 2–4 · breakfast: Martin, Diane, Ethan, and the start choice ──────
[[canvases]]
id   = "opening_breakfast"
name = "Breakfast"
description = "Meets Martin, Diane and Ethan (one flag for the group, F8). The start choice. Sets met_family."

[canvases.trigger]
location      = "kitchen"
is_repeatable = false
priority      = 11
is_active     = true

[[canvases.trigger.schedules]]
weekdays   = [0]
start_time = "07:00"
end_time   = "08:30"

[canvases.trigger.conditions]
version = "1.0"
logic   = "AND"
items = [
  { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "opening_boot", operator = "is_true" },
  { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "met_family",   operator = "is_false" },
]

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "kitchen"
name = "The kitchen"
blocks = [
  { type = "image", props = { file = "scenes/opening_breakfast.jpg", description = "A family kitchen at breakfast, an older man in a suit reading a paper at the head of the table", search_queries = ["family breakfast table man in suit newspaper", "kitchen breakfast morning family"] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "Your stepfather Martin is at the head of the table in a grey suit, reading the paper. He's fifty-two, a partner at Callahan Reed, and he owns everything in this kitchen, including the chair you sit in." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "First day. Callahan wants you in at ten, not nine. Don't be early, and don't be late." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "Your mother Diane puts a plate in front of you. She's his assistant at the firm. She's been up since six, and she's already nervous for you." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_diane" }, content = "Eat something, sweetheart. And say thank you to Martin. He didn't have to do any of this." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "player" }, content = "Thank you, Martin." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "Friday, Emma." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "That's all he says. His eyes stay on you a beat too long, down to your blouse and back up, and then he turns the page." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "choices"

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "Pour your coffee."
targetType = "node"
nodeId     = "opening_breakfast.ethan"

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "ethan"
name = "Ethan"
blocks = [
  { type = "paragraph", content = "Your step-brother Ethan comes in already dressed for the firm, a junior associate two years in. He's twenty-five, and he has hated you since the day you moved in. He leans on the counter and watches you pour." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_ethan" }, content = "So. The intern. We both know how you got this job." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "He says it to your face, but his eyes drop to your legs as you sit, and he looks away too fast. Martin doesn't look up. Your mother goes very still at the stove. Everyone is waiting to see what you say." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "choices"

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "\"I earned it.\""
targetType = "node"

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]

targetType = "node"

flagEffects = [ { targetType = "player", flag = "day1_said_so_what", op = "set" } ]

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "Say nothing."
targetType = "node"
nodeId     = "opening_breakfast.react_nothing"
flagEffects = [ { targetType = "player", flag = "day1_said_nothing", op = "set" } ]

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "react_earned"
name = "\"I earned it.\""
blocks = [
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_ethan" }, content = "Earned it. Right. I'll look forward to seeing that." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "He smirks, but he doesn't look away from you. You don't look away either, and your face is hot." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "Enough. Both of you, out." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "location"
text = "Grab your bag and catch the bus."

[canvases.nodes.exit_block.config]
destinationType          = "specific"
locationId               = "firm"
time_progression_minutes = 165
flagEffects = [ { targetType = "player", flag = "met_family", op = "set" } ]

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "react_so_what"
name = "\"So what?\""
blocks = [
  { type = "paragraph", content = "Ethan blinks. He was ready for you to deny it." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_ethan" }, content = "Wow. At least you're honest about it." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "Enough. Both of you, out." },

blocks = [
  { type = "paragraph", content = "You drink your coffee and let the silence sit there. Ethan waits for a comeback that doesn't come." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_ethan" }, content = "Nothing to say? Figures." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_martin" }, content = "Enough. Both of you, out." },

1:# The First Hour — the opening, and the people in it
19:## Contents
38:## F1 · The opening picks one shape and commits

130:### The worked opening — staged open
207:## F1c · A returning player can skip the opening
215:## F2 · Boot and capstone are two canvases
244:## F2b · The opening is SCREENS, and two of them are not ours
277:### The screen walk — the review view that cannot be faked
303:### How long the opening is

397:## F4 · Every live system gets one beat

713:### So a second surface for the same person in the same room is a NODE INSIDE THE FIRST.

content.content:
519	## F5 · Every character's hub sits behind a meeting
520	
521	**The forbidden shape:** a repeatable canvas with `npc =` set whose base node *is* the
522	introduction. The player walks into a room and the character is simply there, the hub's first
523	paragraph standing in for a meeting. The field does the opposite: Shady Deals' [Car Mechanic]
524	opens on `<<if $met_mechanic == 0>>`, so the first visit is the meeting.
525	
526	**The field's answer.** 17 of 27 shipped games carry per-character meeting state, and the strongest
527	one carries it on effectively its whole navigable cast — degrees-of-lewdity keeps a first-time flag
528	on **24 of its 27 registered NPCs** (`C.npc.<Name>.init`, plus older `_intro`/`_seen` flags for the
529	rest), read in conditions 150 times. become-someone gates **presence**, not just dialogue:
530	`<<if $has.metkate is 1 && $kate.loc is "Beach">>` — she is not in the world until she has been met.
531	the-company sets `player.met.sophie` in a passage named `Intro-MeetSophie`.
532	
533	**Re-measured 2026-09-02 over the 25 parseable games, and the second figure is the one that
534	settles it.** 14 games keep an explicitly-named per-character first-contact flag — **9 of the top
535	10 by engagement** — across **209 characters, 188 of them (90%) read inside a condition**:
536	degrees-of-lewdity 78, become-someone 31, corpo-life 30, wasteland-lewdness 20, patriarch 10,
537	lust-for-life 9, destroyer 7, zaras-school-life 7. Conventions differ and the mechanism does not
538	(`$amanda.intro`, `$janet.metFlag`, `$meet_megan`, `$metellie`, `$crowlemet`, `$gwylanSeen`).
539	
540	> ### ⚠️ Not one character in the field is met at turn one.
541	> Every meeting flag in all 14 games, swept for an initialisation to true before play: **zero**.
542	> Three look like exceptions and none is — `become-someone`'s sits in `Start up Interviews`
543	> (mid-game), `corpo-life`'s in `CFO Dinner Init` (a scene), and `degrees-of-lewdity`'s in
544	> `Widgets variablesVersionUpdate`, the **save-migration** widget that back-fills old saves.
545	
546	**And the field gates PRESENCE on it, not just dialogue** — which is the half our engine is missing.
547	`become-someone`'s Beach passage is a location screen listing who is there, and every row asks two
548	questions:
549	
550	```
551	<<if $nami.intro   && $nami.loc   is "Beach">>
552	<<if $amanda.intro is 1 && $amanda.loc is "Beach">>
553	<<if $nicole.intro && $nicole.loc is "Beach">>
554	```
555	
556	`renderNpcPortraits` (`engine.md` §42) does the **located** half and nothing else. `met AND located`
557	is the shape; the meeting flag on the hub's `trigger.conditions` is how you write the other half here.
558	
559	`zaras-school-life` (numbers only) stages the meetings rather than opening them all at once, and
560	the trigger is a counter rather than a door: one meeting waits for the fourth time she has done a
561	routine, another for day 5 **and** a reputation of 10.
562	
563	**The shape to build:**
564	
565	| | |
566	|---|---|
567	| the meeting | `is_repeatable = false` · high `priority` · location-bound · sets one flag on exit |
568	| the hub | `is_repeatable = true` · **`[canvases.trigger] npc =`** set (F5b — the nesting is load-bearing) · gated on that flag · a **different** `name` |
569	
570	> ### The second shape: the hub can hold its own first contact
571	>
572	> Two canvases is the shape to reach for, not the only one the field ships. **`corpo-life`**
573	> (1,464 comments) opens *Mia Office Interaction* with `<<if $metmia is 0>>` and gates everything
574	> after on `$metkaren is 1` — **one canvas: the first visit is the meeting, every visit after is
575	> the hub.** `become-taxi-driver` and `amore` do the same.
576	>
577	> The rule underneath both is **first contact is gated and happens once**. The canvas count was
578	> never the point. Use the two-canvas shape by default — it keeps the meeting's prose off a screen
579	> the player re-enters forty times, which is `register.md`'s whole argument — and use the one-canvas
580	> shape when the meeting is two lines and a door.
581	>
582	> ⚠️ **The gate cannot see the second shape, and this is the honest statement of that.** A detector
583	> was built and reverted the same hour: the only rule available to it — *"the canvas branches on a
584	> flag it also sets"* — is satisfied by **every day cap** and every arc rung as well. Nothing in
585	> the TOML distinguishes *first contact* from *third rung*: both read a flag `is_false` and set it
586	> on the way out. A lenient check would silently pass
587	> games that really are cold-spawning, which is worse than under-reporting. **So if you build the
588	> one-canvas shape, `every hub is met first` will under-count you — record it in the ledger and
589	> move on.** Field study: `~/Documents/Opening_And_Introduction_Study_20260902/`.
590	
591	**Where a character has several hubs**, the meeting flag belongs on the **first** one — the hub
592	the player reaches first. A later rung can be gated on something downstream instead (`nora_loop`
593	on `nora_stage gte 3`, `canvas_paul_arrangement` on `paul_drinks_done`) and that is correct
594	work. What is never correct is a hub with **no conditions at all**: it puts that character's
595	portrait on a location screen from turn one, however well the first hub is gated.
596	
597	A non-repeatable canvas renders **no portrait** — `selectNpcPortraitCanvasesForLocation` skips
598	`if (!c.isRepeatable) continue` (`v2.py:4884-4889`) — so the meeting cannot leak onto the location
599	screen as a face, and the hub cannot appear before the meeting has fired.
600	
601	> ### ⚠️ `requires_npc` does NOT gate the auto-fire path. This corrects v1.
602	>
603	> `npc-intro.md` §1.3 says to set `requires_npc` so the meeting *"fires where the NPC is."* Traced
604	> in the engine, that is **false** for a canvas that auto-fires:
605	>
606	> ```
607	> getStoryCanvasRedirect              v2.py:5826
608	>   -> selectAutoFireCanvasForLocation    v2.py:5313
609	>     -> isCanvasValid                    v2.py:5477
610	>        checks: schedules · conditions · repeatability.  requiresNpc is never read.
611	> ```
612	>
613	> `requiresNpc` is emitted at `v2.py:13348` and read on the random-encounter selector
614	> (`v2.py:6412`), the substitution rules (`v2.py:6491`), and — through `setup._npcPresentForCanvas`
615	> (`v2.py:5653`) — the solo lane (`v2.py:5594`, `:6243`) and the launcher (`v2.py:3503`).
616	> **None of them is auto-fire.**
617	>
618	> Consequence: a meeting bound to a bar with `requires_npc`, whose character's schedule puts him
619	> there only in the evening, auto-fires whenever the player walks in with the other conditions
620	> met — so the prose can introduce him in an empty bar at ten in the morning.
621	>
622	> **Gate the meeting on a `schedules` window that matches where the character actually is, or on a
623	> flag the player can only hold by having been there.** Keep `requires_npc` as well — it is free,
624	> it is correct on the paths that read it, and it documents intent — but never rely on it alone.
625	
626	> **Gated as `a meeting fires where they are` (G38).**
627	>
628	> ⚠️ **When doctrine and the schema comment disagree, the schema wins, because the schema is what
629	> is open while you type.** `template_import.py` once described `requires_npc` as something that
630	> *"lets authors drop per-canvas location+time gates"*, with no scope on the claim — false for
631	> every meeting canvas. The comment is corrected (`template_import.py:810`); the gate is why it
632	> cannot come back.
633	
634	---
635	
636	## F5b · The portrait is the presence gate, and the key that makes it is `[canvases.trigger] npc`
637	
638	F5 says the hub carries `npc =`. **It goes at the top level of `[canvases.trigger]`, and the
639	nesting is the whole rule.**
640	
641	```toml
642	[[canvases]]
643	id   = "hub_theo_garage"
644	name = "Sit with him"
645	# npc = "npc_theo"        ← WRONG. Silently discarded.
646	
647	[canvases.trigger]
648	location = "the_garage"
649	npc      = "npc_theo"     # ← RIGHT.
650	```
651	
652	`TemplateCanvas` has four content fields and `npc` is not one of them
653	(`template_import.py:958-965`), and it is built with named arguments only
654	(`:2397-2405`), so a canvas-level `npc` key is dropped with **no error, no warning, and a green
655	build**. The field the engine reads is `TemplateTrigger.npc` (`:677`), carried through
656	`game_graph.py:311` into trigger metadata, out at `v2.py:12205`, and emitted as `npcId`
657	(`v2.py:12262`).
658	
659	**Three things ride on that one key, and all three fail together.**
660	
661	1. **The face.** `renderNpcPortraits` and its selector both bail on `if (!c.npcId) continue`
662	   (`v2.py:5560`, `v2.py:5079`). No `npcId` anywhere in a game means `renderNpcPortraits` returns
663	   the empty string at every location, for every hour, for the whole run.
664	2. **The presence gate.** The portrait renderer is where a character's hours are actually enforced:
665	   it reads their declared `[[npcs.schedules]]` and compares `getNpcLocation` to where the player is
666	   standing (`v2.py:5596-5599`). Lose the portrait and you lose the check — the surface stays
667	   clickable in an empty room at any hour.
668	3. **The label.** A canvas with no `npcId` falls through to the solo path, which does not skip it
669	   (`v2.py:5679`) and writes the canvas's own `displayName` straight into the link
670	   (`v2.py:5710`). The portrait path would have written the resolved character name. So the title
671	   you wrote for the author's benefit becomes the words on the player's screen — `@` tokens and all,
672	   because `name` is not a field the engine resolves tokens in (`engine.md` §43).
673	
674	> ### ⚠️ `requires_npc` is a different field. It gates the row; it does not draw the face.
675	>
676	> **Corrected 2026-09-03.** It is now read on three paths — `trigger_mode = "random"`,
677	> `substitution_only`, and **the solo lane**, through `setup._npcPresentForCanvas`. A solo-lane row
678	> carrying it renders only while that character is standing where the player is. It still does
679	> **not** gate the auto-fire path (`engine.md` §31), and it still draws no portrait.
680	>
681	> A hub carrying `requires_npc` and no `npc` still has no face and no portrait window. Where a
682	> person-bound surface genuinely should not be a portrait — an activity that happens in a place
683	> while somebody is around, rather than a surface on that person — `requires_npc` now does the
684	> presence half on its own, and `trigger.schedules` remains what narrows it to a *time*.
685	
686	A game with `npc` on `[[canvases]]` for every character surface ships with zero portraits: every
687	character renders as a text link carrying the canvas's own name, and every character's hours are
688	enforced nowhere. The copyable block in `templates/first-hour.toml` carries `npc` under
689	`[canvases.trigger]`; the only other `npc =` example in the skill is `[[phone.daily_topics]]`,
690	where it genuinely is a top-level key.
691	
692	> **Gated as `no canvas key is discarded`.** Fails on any key sitting on `[[canvases]]` that is not
693	> one of the seven `TemplateCanvas` fields (`template_import.py:1043-1049`). It invents no threshold
694	> and cannot produce a false positive: such a key does nothing at all, so writing one is never
695	> correct.
696	>
697	> ⚠️ **The class is the placement, not the key.** `substitution_only` one level too high fails the
698	> same way: the walk-in renders as a clickable activity instead of a dispatcher-only target. So the
699	> gate checks every key, not `npc` alone.
700	>
701	> The companion lint **`bound to a person, no face`** carries the softer case — a repeatable
702	> `requires_npc` canvas with no `trigger.npc` — as a **list, never a score**. A walk-in, or a scene
703	> that happens in a place while somebody is around, legitimately has this shape, often already
704	> windowed by its own `trigger.schedules`; a gate here would fail games for obeying the doctrine.
705	
706	⚠️ **One location shows one canvas per character.** The renderer collects every valid repeatable
707	canvas for an NPC and keeps the highest `priority`, preferring affordable over cost-blocked
708	(`v2.py:5545-5578`). Three surfaces for one person in one room is not three rows — it is one face
709	showing whichever ranks highest right now. That is the intended shape and it composes with the
710	tier ladder, but decide the priorities on purpose: a hub at 6 sitting under an escalation at 7 means
711	the escalation replaces it whenever its conditions hold.
712	
713	### So a second surface for the same person in the same room is a NODE INSIDE THE FIRST.
714	
715	Written as its own canvas, a talk screen cannot take `npc` without the hub swallowing it (the
716	selector keeps one canvas per character, `v2.py:5362-5366`), so it lands in the solo lane — the one
717	that holds Sleep and Shower and attaches no name to anything — with its button text as its only
718	identity. Folding it into the hub does not bury it: **a node has no priority.** Priority ranks
719	canvases competing for one face. A node is reached by a choice.
720	
721	```toml
722	# on the hub's base exit_block — no effects, no clock. It is a door, not an act (the-surfaces.md R7)
723	[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
724	text       = "Ask him about the car."
725	targetType = "node"
726	nodeId     = "talk"
727	```
728	
729	⚠️ **And when a HIGHER-priority canvas for the same character owns that room, the branch retires
730	with the hub unless something links to it.** `act_garage_late` (p7) replaces `hub_theo_garage` (p6)
731	the moment its arc flag sets, so the pool folded into the hub goes dark exactly when the player has
732	most reason to want it. A **qualified** nodeId reaches across canvases —
733	`nodeId = "hub_theo_garage.talk"` — resolved globally at import (`template_import.py:7973-7979`,
734	validated at `:4623-4643`). One line on the escalation's base, and the two surfaces share the pool
735	instead of duplicating forty lines of dialogue.
736	
737	⚠️ **Check which phase file the surface lives in before you decide it is safe.**
738	`merge_toml_phases.py` drops `6_dev_shortcuts.toml` **by name** on `--no-dev` (`:62`), which is the
739	release setting (`:80`). Anything authored there is gone from the released game.
740	
741	---
742	
743	## F6 · A meeting is small, and somebody speaks
744	
745	Measured across 696 passages named intro/meet in 18 field games:
746	
747	```
748	median 101 words · quartiles 57 / 101 / 194 · 66% under 150 words · 64% carry spoken dialogue
749	```
750	
751	Narrowing to passages named *meet* only (158 of them): median **166**, **55%** spoken. Both
752	instruments land in the same band.
753	
754	the-company's entire first meeting with the player's employer is **80 words**:
755	
756	> *"Your new employer stands and leans forward to shake your hand. This close you notice her
757	> piercing violet eyes as she appears to size you up behind a sincere yet cunning smile."*
758	
759	Role, then the look, then a beat. That is the whole thing.
760	
761	**Where the player cannot yet know the name**, set `speaker = "unknown"` on the `dialog` block and
762	the engine prints **"Stranger:"** (`v2.py:15212-15218`); switch to the NPC speaker once names have
763	been exchanged.
764	
765	⚠️ **A meeting with no `dialog` block is not a meeting.** The person is in the room. If they do not
766	say anything, the player has been handed a description, not an introduction. This is `register.md`
767	S3 applied at the one moment it matters most.
768	
769	---
770	
771	## F7 · Role before name
772	
773	The field's ordering, in the clearest case:
774	
775	> *"Your new employer stands and leans forward to shake your hand."* — the-company
776	
777	**Relationship label first, then the name.** The label is what the player can hold; the name is
778	what they will need later.
779	
780	**The strongest form of this rule is mechanical, and it is worth stealing.** degrees-of-lewdity
781	swaps the description for the name once the meeting flag is set, so the game literally cannot use a
782	name the player has not earned:
783	
784	```
785	deliver a letter to <<if $wren_intro is undefined>>a <gender> named Wren.  <He> can be found at
786	  Remy's estate in the moor, or at the docks at night<<else>>Wren<</if>>.
787	```
788	
789	Ours has the same primitive: a `[group]` block with `conditions` on the meeting flag, or a
790	`cascade`. Use it where the reference is load-bearing — a quest card, a guidance line, a location
791	description that sends the player somewhere.
792	
793	⚠️ **Honest limit.** The naming swap is heaviest in one game (64 blocks in degrees-of-lewdity;
794	course-of-temptation 9, amore 2). It is the strongest game's mechanism, not a field-wide norm — so
795	it is a **tool to reach for**, not a bar the gates hold you to. The **flag** is the norm; the swap
796	is what a good author does with it.
797	
798	⚠️ **NOTHING ENFORCES THIS AT THE MEETING ITSELF, which is the one place it matters most.** The
799	`named before met` lint asks only whether a character's name appears in the opening, a quest card
800	or a room description *before* they have a meeting — and it skips anyone who has one outright
801	(`gates.py`, `if n["id"] in has_meeting: continue`). It never reads the meeting's own text. So a
802	meeting that opens on a bare name passes every check in this skill.
803	
804	**And a check for it was tried and rejected**, which is worth recording so it is not re-attempted
805	blind: a kinship-word detector fires on every cast that is not family, where the word was never
806	going to be there, and on mid-arc canvases that are not introductions. Most of its hits are wrong.
807	**Read the first line of every meeting yourself.** It is five lines of reading per game.
808	
809	---
810	
811	## F8 · The flag belongs to a scene that meets them
812	
813	The dodge this rule exists to kill: gate the whole cast on one flag set by a scene that meets
814	**none** of them (`doors_open`), and every hub is technically "behind a meeting" while the cast
815	still arrives cold.
816	
817	**A meeting flag counts for a character only if the one-time scene that sets it names them** —
818	binds them, or gives them a line. A group scene that meets three people and sets one flag meets all
819	three. A flag set by a scene that names nobody meets nobody. A character named in the **forced**
820	opening — bound to the starting canvas or a capstone it reaches, or speaking on its first screen —
821	is met by playing the game, and their hub needs no gate.
822	
823	*(LO decided, 2026-09-28.)* Three of the four passing games meet every character before their hub
824	is reachable: Shady Deals (a trio met in one scene, on one flag), Cupid's Way (the office tour) and
825	In Her Own Hands. Course of Temptation does it differently: its generic "Talk to" works on
826	strangers. So this rule is a choice backed by field evidence, not a universal law.
827	
828	⚠️ **Sequence the cast in waves.** Not everyone is reachable on day one. Stage the entrances so each
829	arrival is a punctuation mark. For a character who arrives mid-game, **withhold their schedule until
830	the meeting fires** — `getNpcsWithSchedules` (`v2.py:3886`) surfaces every declared NPC on the
831	Schedule page from day one regardless of any gate, so a schedule given early spoils the entrance.
832	
833	### The same flag belongs on that character's quest cards
834	
835	F5 through F8 gate the **canvases**. They say nothing about the **guidance surface**: a Quests page
836	that lists every character on click one — names, the room each stands in, the hour they are there —
837	spoils every meeting in the game. The field keeps the name back until the meeting: In Her Own
838	Hands' [Progress_Hints_Base], behind `<<if not $xr.ab.m>>`, gives only *"I should check out some of
839	the local shops . . ."*
840	
841	**A character's `[[quest_cards]]` carry that character's meeting flag in `when`.**
842	
843	```toml
844	when = [ { flag = "met_wade", subject = "player", op = "is_true" },
845	         { trait = "want", subject = "npc", npc_id = "npc_wade", op = "lt", value = 40 } ]
846	```
847	
848	The engine already does the rest. `QuestsPage` wraps each character's section in `<<if _card>>`
849	(`v2.py:17070`) and `setup.pickQuestsCard` returns `null` when no card's `when` matches
850	(`v2.py:16829`), so an unmet character renders **no heading and no section** — the roster fills in
851	as the player meets people, which is what the field ships (the-company's cast table is
852	`<<if $player.met[_char.id]>>` per row).
853	
854	Three things to get right:
855	
856	- **A `when` item sets `flag` *or* `trait`, never both** — the importer rejects an item carrying
857	  both (`template_import.py:5710`). The meeting flag is its own item beside the trait band.
858	- **Put it on *every* card in that character's ladder**, not just the first. A gap means the
859	  character reappears at the band whose card you missed.
860	- **Flag names are not validated against anything.** Nothing checks that `met_wade` exists; a typo
861	  hides that character's guidance forever and no build error says so. Read the name off the
862	  meeting canvas's own `flagEffects`, not off memory.
863	
864	⚠️ **This flag is load-bearing twice.** The cast page (`[ui.cast_page]`, `engine.md` §34) lists a
865	character exactly when `pickQuestsCard` returns a card for them, so one flag reveals both surfaces
866	and they cannot fall out of step. The cost is worth stating plainly: **a character with no quest
867	card can never appear on the cast page.** `guidance exists` already requires every `[[npcs]]` entry
868	to carry one, so this cannot happen in a game that passes its own scoreboard.
869	
870	**Story-goal cards — the ones with no `npc_id` — are never gated this way.** They are the
871	always-live "Story Goals" section, and a guidance page whose every card is gated renders
872	"No active quests." on turn one.
873	
874	---
875	
876	## F9 · A place says what it is on the screen the player keeps coming back to
877	
878	**The location's own `description` says what kind of place this is and what happens here.** Not a
879	scene that plays once. The description is the only surface the player sees on *every* visit,
880	including the twentieth, and "what is this place" is a standing question, not a first-entry one.
881	
882	**The field names the function on the room screen itself.** Shady Deals' [Pawnshop] renders, on
883	every visit, *"Pawnshop might buy various electronics and jewelry."* — what the place is, and what
884	the player does there, in one line.
885	
886	⚠️ **This is `register.md`'s "words the player has to already own", one level up.** There the unit
887	was a word; here it is a whole place. A location whose *function* is only implied is an unglossed
888	noun the size of a room.
889	
890	### The field's device is the room screen, and it changes
891	
892	Measured across the 26-game corpus:
893	
894	```
895	                                    field median
896	room prose the player sees per visit   82 words
897	variant branches per room screen           10
898	rooms that rotate their text              22%
899	rooms that vary by hour                   17%
900	an event renders ON the room screen       yes
901	```
902	
903	The place tells its own story every time you walk in, and it is not the same story twice.
904	
905	### ⚠️ The first-visit canvas is a MINORITY device — do not reach for it first
906	
907	This section previously taught the opposite, and worked its example from
908	`degrees-of-lewdity`'s `$forest_shop_intro` / `$gwylan_cafe_intro` family. Counted properly, that
909	family is **one game**:
910	
911	```
912	degrees-of-lewdity   258 first-visit branches, 117 flags     the only game doing it
913	realm-of-corruption   12
914	amore · patriarch · sluttown-usa · zaras-school-life · new-life-project     2 each
915	EIGHTEEN OF TWENTY-SIX GAMES     zero
916	  — including destroyer, become-someone, course-of-temptation, the-company, friends-of-mine
917	```
918	
919	It is a legitimate device and DoL builds a great deal on it. **It is not the default and it does not
920	substitute for a description that names the function**, because it plays once and the confusion it
921	is aimed at is permanent. LO ruled on exactly that ground:
922	
923	> LO: *"I think the place name is description and what was going in that place should be able to
924	> tell the whole story."*
925	
926	Reach for a first visit when a place has a **one-time** thing to say — a door that was locked and
927	now is not, a room whose meaning changes the first time you are let into it. Never as the place's
928	only introduction.
929	
930	### Authoring the two halves
931	
932	**State-variance — `[[locations.description_variants]]`, shipped 2026-08-26.** The base
933	`description` stays required and becomes the else; each variant is `{conditions, text}` and the
934	engine emits a first-match chain. Conditions are the ordinary ones, so the most useful axis is
935	**who is in the room** — which is the "what happens here" half of the rule, told by the room itself:
936	
937	```toml
938	[[locations]]
939	id          = "the_yard"
940	description = "Gravel from the back step of the house to the roller door of the shop…"
941	
942	[[locations.description_variants]]
943	conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [
944	  { type = "npc_at_location", location_id = "the_shop_floor", operator = "is_present" },
945	] }
946	text = "…and the roller door is up. Air tools go in bursts and stop."
947	```
948	
949	⚠️ **`version = "1.0"` is not optional.** `triggerConditionsSatisfied` returns **true** for any
950	`conditions{}` without it, so a variant missing it renders forever and the location's own
951	description is never seen again. The importer refuses it rather than building green.
952	
953	⚠️ **There is no time-of-day condition.** The evaluator has `flag`, `trait`, `npc_at_location`,
954	`stage`, `quest`, `item`, `days_since_flag`, `corruption_level` and the clothing family — and
955	nothing that reads the hour. So the field's 17%-vary-by-hour column is still **not authorable**;
956	schedules gate canvases by time, not descriptions. Gate presence-variants on who is there instead,
957	which is where the hour shows up anyway.
958	
959	⚠️ **A random ambient still takes the WHOLE screen, and that is an engine limit, not a choice.**
960	When a Lane 2 ambient rolls on entry the room `<<goto>>`s to it — no title, no description, no
961	portraits, no exits — so on that visit the description does not render at all. An `ambient_render =
962	"inline"` setting that gave the ambient the description slot instead was built and **reverted on
963	2026-08-26**; do not write doctrine or a ledger promise against it. `destroyer` renders its
964	encounter in the description position and keeps its affordance bar and exits either way, so the
965	shape is known and the gap is real — it is simply not available today.
966	
967	### Rotation is still not built
968	
969	The field's other column — 22% of rooms rotating their text between visits — needs a per-visit
970	counter like `block_pool`'s and does not exist for descriptions. Do not promise it in a ledger.
971	
972	---
973	
974	## F10 · The role stays attached after the introduction
975	
976	F7 gets the role onto the screen at the meeting. **F9 says a place keeps saying what it is on every
977	visit. This is the same rule for people, and it is the one that was missing.**
978	
979	"Who is this" is a **standing** question. A meeting answers it once, and the player then spends forty
980	visits in a hub where the man is a bare first name.
981	
982	**Lint `the role stays attached`** (gates.py:5519) takes each character's anchor words from his own
983	`npcs[].relationship` line and counts how often his own canvases use them, per 10k words. It prints a
984	list, thinnest first, with no bar. It counts every canvas bound to him, so a re-entered surface and a
985	one-shot count the same. Reading which is which is yours.
986	
987	**Where it goes: the surfaces the player RE-ENTERS.** A hub, an ambient, a walk-in. Not the one-shot
988	that introduced him — that one is already doing its job.
989	
990	**Both, never one instead of the other.**
991	
992	> *"Relation and name both are important and both can't be replaced with another. We are not calling
993	> out for replacing one with another."*
994	
995	⚠️ **Do not swap the name out for the relation on the speaker line.** `destroyer` does
996	(`<<speech "teagan" "Stepsister">>`) and it is the only game in the 26-game corpus that does — it
997	survives it by having **exactly one of each relation**. Relation words on buttons run at **field
998	median 0.4%, max 2.0%**. `sluttown-usa` is a family premise with 37,408 speaker labels and uses **names only**. Swapping does not remove the memory tax,
999	it moves it: the player now has to remember who "Stepsister" is.
1000	
1001	The cheap form is three words riding in prose that was going to be there anyway: name and relation on
1002	the same line, at the point of use, and the register does not move.
1003	
1004	**Put it in a `block_pool` variant rather than in the always-renders text.** A hub pool cycles, so
1005	the anchor recurs periodically instead of arriving every single visit, which is how a reminder turns
1006	into nagging.
1007	
1008	### The mechanical half — `npcs[].role`

## F5 · Every character's hub sits behind a meeting

**The forbidden shape:** a repeatable canvas with `npc =` set whose base node *is* the
introduction. The player walks into a room and the character is simply there, the hub's first
paragraph standing in for a meeting. The field does the opposite: Shady Deals' [Car Mechanic]
opens on `<<if $met_mechanic == 0>>`, so the first visit is the meeting.

**The field's answer.** 17 of 27 shipped games carry per-character meeting state, and the strongest
one carries it on effectively its whole navigable cast — degrees-of-lewdity keeps a first-time flag
on **24 of its 27 registered NPCs** (`C.npc.<Name>.init`, plus older `_intro`/`_seen` flags for the
rest), read in conditions 150 times. become-someone gates **presence**, not just dialogue:
`<<if $has.metkate is 1 && $kate.loc is "Beach">>` — she is not in the world until she has been met.
the-company sets `player.met.sophie` in a passage named `Intro-MeetSophie`.

**Re-measured 2026-09-02 over the 25 parseable games, and the second figure is the one that
settles it.** 14 games keep an explicitly-named per-character first-contact flag — **9 of the top
10 by engagement** — across **209 characters, 188 of them (90%) read inside a condition**:
degrees-of-lewdity 78, become-someone 31, corpo-life 30, wasteland-lewdness 20, patriarch 10,
lust-for-life 9, destroyer 7, zaras-school-life 7. Conventions differ and the mechanism does not
(`$amanda.intro`, `$janet.metFlag`, `$meet_megan`, `$metellie`, `$crowlemet`, `$gwylanSeen`).

> ### ⚠️ Not one character in the field is met at turn one.
> Every meeting flag in all 14 games, swept for an initialisation to true before play: **zero**.
> Three look like exceptions and none is — `become-someone`'s sits in `Start up Interviews`
> (mid-game), `corpo-life`'s in `CFO Dinner Init` (a scene), and `degrees-of-lewdity`'s in
> `Widgets variablesVersionUpdate`, the **save-migration** widget that back-fills old saves.

**And the field gates PRESENCE on it, not just dialogue** — which is the half our engine is missing.
`become-someone`'s Beach passage is a location screen listing who is there, and every row asks two
questions:

```
<<if $nami.intro   && $nami.loc   is "Beach">>
<<if $amanda.intro is 1 && $amanda.loc is "Beach">>
<<if $nicole.intro && $nicole.loc is "Beach">>
```

`renderNpcPortraits` (`engine.md` §42) does the **located** half and nothing else. `met AND located`
is the shape; the meeting flag on the hub's `trigger.conditions` is how you write the other half here.

`zaras-school-life` (numbers only) stages the meetings rather than opening them all at once, and
the trigger is a counter rather than a door: one meeting waits for the fourth time she has done a
routine, another for day 5 **and** a reputation of 10.

**The shape to build:**

| | |
|---|---|
| the meeting | `is_repeatable = false` · high `priority` · location-bound · sets one flag on exit |
| the hub | `is_repeatable = true` · **`[canvases.trigger] npc =`** set (F5b — the nesting is load-bearing) · gated on that flag · a **different** `name` |

> ### The second shape: the hub can hold its own first contact
>
> Two canvases is the shape to reach for, not the only one the field ships. **`corpo-life`**
> (1,464 comments) opens *Mia Office Interaction* with `<<if $metmia is 0>>` and gates everything
> after on `$metkaren is 1` — **one canvas: the first visit is the meeting, every visit after is
> the hub.** `become-taxi-driver` and `amore` do the same.
>
> The rule underneath both is **first contact is gated and happens once**. The canvas count was
> never the point. Use the two-canvas shape by default — it keeps the meeting's prose off a screen
> the player re-enters forty times, which is `register.md`'s whole argument — and use the one-canvas
> shape when the meeting is two lines and a door.
>
> ⚠️ **The gate cannot see the second shape, and this is the honest statement of that.** A detector
> was built and reverted the same hour: the only rule available to it — *"the canvas branches on a
> flag it also sets"* — is satisfied by **every day cap** and every arc rung as well. Nothing in
> the TOML distinguishes *first contact* from *third rung*: both read a flag `is_false` and set it
> on the way out. A lenient check would silently pass
> games that really are cold-spawning, which is worse than under-reporting. **So if you build the
> one-canvas shape, `every hub is met first` will under-count you — record it in the ledger and
> move on.** Field study: `~/Documents/Opening_And_Introduction_Study_20260902/`.

**Where a character has several hubs**, the meeting flag belongs on the **first** one — the hub
the player reaches first. A later rung can be gated on something downstream instead (`nora_loop`
on `nora_stage gte 3`, `canvas_paul_arrangement` on `paul_drinks_done`) and that is correct
work. What is never correct is a hub with **no conditions at all**: it puts that character's
portrait on a location screen from turn one, however well the first hub is gated.

A non-repeatable canvas renders **no portrait** — `selectNpcPortraitCanvasesForLocation` skips
`if (!c.isRepeatable) continue` (`v2.py:4884-4889`) — so the meeting cannot leak onto the location
screen as a face, and the hub cannot appear before the meeting has fired.

> ### ⚠️ `requires_npc` does NOT gate the auto-fire path. This corrects v1.
>
> `npc-intro.md` §1.3 says to set `requires_npc` so the meeting *"fires where the NPC is."* Traced
> in the engine, that is **false** for a canvas that auto-fires:
>
> ```
> getStoryCanvasRedirect              v2.py:5826
>   -> selectAutoFireCanvasForLocation    v2.py:5313
>     -> isCanvasValid                    v2.py:5477
>        checks: schedules · conditions · repeatability.  requiresNpc is never read.
> ```
>
> `requiresNpc` is emitted at `v2.py:13348` and read on the random-encounter selector
> (`v2.py:6412`), the substitution rules (`v2.py:6491`), and — through `setup._npcPresentForCanvas`
> (`v2.py:5653`) — the solo lane (`v2.py:5594`, `:6243`) and the launcher (`v2.py:3503`).
> **None of them is auto-fire.**
>
> Consequence: a meeting bound to a bar with `requires_npc`, whose character's schedule puts him
> there only in the evening, auto-fires whenever the player walks in with the other conditions
> met — so the prose can introduce him in an empty bar at ten in the morning.
>
> **Gate the meeting on a `schedules` window that matches where the character actually is, or on a
> flag the player can only hold by having been there.** Keep `requires_npc` as well — it is free,
> it is correct on the paths that read it, and it documents intent — but never rely on it alone.

> **Gated as `a meeting fires where they are` (G38).**
>
> ⚠️ **When doctrine and the schema comment disagree, the schema wins, because the schema is what
> is open while you type.** `template_import.py` once described `requires_npc` as something that
> *"lets authors drop per-canvas location+time gates"*, with no scope on the claim — false for
> every meeting canvas. The comment is corrected (`template_import.py:810`); the gate is why it
> cannot come back.

---

## F5b · The portrait is the presence gate, and the key that makes it is `[canvases.trigger] npc`

F5 says the hub carries `npc =`. **It goes at the top level of `[canvases.trigger]`, and the
nesting is the whole rule.**

```toml
[[canvases]]
id   = "hub_theo_garage"
name = "Sit with him"
# npc = "npc_theo"        ← WRONG. Silently discarded.

[canvases.trigger]
location = "the_garage"
npc      = "npc_theo"     # ← RIGHT.
```

`TemplateCanvas` has four content fields and `npc` is not one of them
(`template_import.py:958-965`), and it is built with named arguments only
(`:2397-2405`), so a canvas-level `npc` key is dropped with **no error, no warning, and a green
build**. The field the engine reads is `TemplateTrigger.npc` (`:677`), carried through
`game_graph.py:311` into trigger metadata, out at `v2.py:12205`, and emitted as `npcId`
(`v2.py:12262`).

**Three things ride on that one key, and all three fail together.**

1. **The face.** `renderNpcPortraits` and its selector both bail on `if (!c.npcId) continue`
   (`v2.py:5560`, `v2.py:5079`). No `npcId` anywhere in a game means `renderNpcPortraits` returns
   the empty string at every location, for every hour, for the whole run.
2. **The presence gate.** The portrait renderer is where a character's hours are actually enforced:
   it reads their declared `[[npcs.schedules]]` and compares `getNpcLocation` to where the player is
   standing (`v2.py:5596-5599`). Lose the portrait and you lose the check — the surface stays
   clickable in an empty room at any hour.
3. **The label.** A canvas with no `npcId` falls through to the solo path, which does not skip it
   (`v2.py:5679`) and writes the canvas's own `displayName` straight into the link
   (`v2.py:5710`). The portrait path would have written the resolved character name. So the title
   you wrote for the author's benefit becomes the words on the player's screen — `@` tokens and all,
   because `name` is not a field the engine resolves tokens in (`engine.md` §43).

> ### ⚠️ `requires_npc` is a different field. It gates the row; it does not draw the face.
>
> **Corrected 2026-09-03.** It is now read on three paths — `trigger_mode = "random"`,
> `substitution_only`, and **the solo lane**, through `setup._npcPresentForCanvas`. A solo-lane row
> carrying it renders only while that character is standing where the player is. It still does
> **not** gate the auto-fire path (`engine.md` §31), and it still draws no portrait.
>
> A hub carrying `requires_npc` and no `npc` still has no face and no portrait window. Where a
> person-bound surface genuinely should not be a portrait — an activity that happens in a place
> while somebody is around, rather than a surface on that person — `requires_npc` now does the
> presence half on its own, and `trigger.schedules` remains what narrows it to a *time*.

A game with `npc` on `[[canvases]]` for every character surface ships with zero portraits: every
character renders as a text link carrying the canvas's own name, and every character's hours are
enforced nowhere. The copyable block in `templates/first-hour.toml` carries `npc` under
`[canvases.trigger]`; the only other `npc =` example in the skill is `[[phone.daily_topics]]`,
where it genuinely is a top-level key.

> **Gated as `no canvas key is discarded`.** Fails on any key sitting on `[[canvases]]` that is not
> one of the seven `TemplateCanvas` fields (`template_import.py:1043-1049`). It invents no threshold
> and cannot produce a false positive: such a key does nothing at all, so writing one is never
> correct.
>
> ⚠️ **The class is the placement, not the key.** `substitution_only` one level too high fails the
> same way: the walk-in renders as a clickable activity instead of a dispatcher-only target. So the
> gate checks every key, not `npc` alone.
>
> The companion lint **`bound to a person, no face`** carries the softer case — a repeatable
> `requires_npc` canvas with no `trigger.npc` — as a **list, never a score**. A walk-in, or a scene
> that happens in a place while somebody is around, legitimately has this shape, often already
> windowed by its own `trigger.schedules`; a gate here would fail games for obeying the doctrine.

⚠️ **One location shows one canvas per character.** The renderer collects every valid repeatable
canvas for an NPC and keeps the highest `priority`, preferring affordable over cost-blocked
(`v2.py:5545-5578`). Three surfaces for one person in one room is not three rows — it is one face
showing whichever ranks highest right now. That is the intended shape and it composes with the
tier ladder, but decide the priorities on purpose: a hub at 6 sitting under an escalation at 7 means
the escalation replaces it whenever its conditions hold.

### So a second surface for the same person in the same room is a NODE INSIDE THE FIRST.

Written as its own canvas, a talk screen cannot take `npc` without the hub swallowing it (the
selector keeps one canvas per character, `v2.py:5362-5366`), so it lands in the solo lane — the one
that holds Sleep and Shower and attaches no name to anything — with its button text as its only
identity. Folding it into the hub does not bury it: **a node has no priority.** Priority ranks
canvases competing for one face. A node is reached by a choice.

```toml
# on the hub's base exit_block — no effects, no clock. It is a door, not an act (the-surfaces.md R7)
[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "Ask him about the car."
targetType = "node"
nodeId     = "talk"
```

⚠️ **And when a HIGHER-priority canvas for the same character owns that room, the branch retires
with the hub unless something links to it.** `act_garage_late` (p7) replaces `hub_theo_garage` (p6)
the moment its arc flag sets, so the pool folded into the hub goes dark exactly when the player has
most reason to want it. A **qualified** nodeId reaches across canvases —
`nodeId = "hub_theo_garage.talk"` — resolved globally at import (`template_import.py:7973-7979`,
validated at `:4623-4643`). One line on the escalation's base, and the two surfaces share the pool
instead of duplicating forty lines of dialogue.

⚠️ **Check which phase file the surface lives in before you decide it is safe.**
`merge_toml_phases.py` drops `6_dev_shortcuts.toml` **by name** on `--no-dev` (`:62`), which is the
release setting (`:80`). Anything authored there is gone from the released game.

---

## F6 · A meeting is small, and somebody speaks

Measured across 696 passages named intro/meet in 18 field games:

```
median 101 words · quartiles 57 / 101 / 194 · 66% under 150 words · 64% carry spoken dialogue
```

Narrowing to passages named *meet* only (158 of them): median **166**, **55%** spoken. Both
instruments land in the same band.

the-company's entire first meeting with the player's employer is **80 words**:

> *"Your new employer stands and leans forward to shake your hand. This close you notice her
> piercing violet eyes as she appears to size you up behind a sincere yet cunning smile."*

Role, then the look, then a beat. That is the whole thing.

**Where the player cannot yet know the name**, set `speaker = "unknown"` on the `dialog` block and
the engine prints **"Stranger:"** (`v2.py:15212-15218`); switch to the NPC speaker once names have
been exchanged.

⚠️ **A meeting with no `dialog` block is not a meeting.** The person is in the room. If they do not
say anything, the player has been handed a description, not an introduction. This is `register.md`
S3 applied at the one moment it matters most.

---

## F7 · Role before name

The field's ordering, in the clearest case:

> *"Your new employer stands and leans forward to shake your hand."* — the-company

**Relationship label first, then the name.** The label is what the player can hold; the name is
what they will need later.

**The strongest form of this rule is mechanical, and it is worth stealing.** degrees-of-lewdity
swaps the description for the name once the meeting flag is set, so the game literally cannot use a
name the player has not earned:

```
deliver a letter to <<if $wren_intro is undefined>>a <gender> named Wren.  <He> can be found at
  Remy's estate in the moor, or at the docks at night<<else>>Wren<</if>>.
```

Ours has the same primitive: a `[group]` block with `conditions` on the meeting flag, or a
`cascade`. Use it where the reference is load-bearing — a quest card, a guidance line, a location
description that sends the player somewhere.

⚠️ **Honest limit.** The naming swap is heaviest in one game (64 blocks in degrees-of-lewdity;
course-of-temptation 9, amore 2). It is the strongest game's mechanism, not a field-wide norm — so
it is a **tool to reach for**, not a bar the gates hold you to. The **flag** is the norm; the swap
is what a good author does with it.

⚠️ **NOTHING ENFORCES THIS AT THE MEETING ITSELF, which is the one place it matters most.** The
`named before met` lint asks only whether a character's name appears in the opening, a quest card
or a room description *before* they have a meeting — and it skips anyone who has one outright
(`gates.py`, `if n["id"] in has_meeting: continue`). It never reads the meeting's own text. So a
meeting that opens on a bare name passes every check in this skill.

**And a check for it was tried and rejected**, which is worth recording so it is not re-attempted
blind: a kinship-word detector fires on every cast that is not family, where the word was never
going to be there, and on mid-arc canvases that are not introductions. Most of its hits are wrong.
**Read the first line of every meeting yourself.** It is five lines of reading per game.

---

## F8 · The flag belongs to a scene that meets them

The dodge this rule exists to kill: gate the whole cast on one flag set by a scene that meets
**none** of them (`doors_open`), and every hub is technically "behind a meeting" while the cast
still arrives cold.

**A meeting flag counts for a character only if the one-time scene that sets it names them** —
binds them, or gives them a line. A group scene that meets three people and sets one flag meets all
three. A flag set by a scene that names nobody meets nobody. A character named in the **forced**
opening — bound to the starting canvas or a capstone it reaches, or speaking on its first screen —
is met by playing the game, and their hub needs no gate.

*(LO decided, 2026-09-28.)* Three of the four passing games meet every character before their hub
is reachable: Shady Deals (a trio met in one scene, on one flag), Cupid's Way (the office tour) and
In Her Own Hands. Course of Temptation does it differently: its generic "Talk to" works on
strangers. So this rule is a choice backed by field evidence, not a universal law.

⚠️ **Sequence the cast in waves.** Not everyone is reachable on day one. Stage the entrances so each
arrival is a punctuation mark. For a character who arrives mid-game, **withhold their schedule until
the meeting fires** — `getNpcsWithSchedules` (`v2.py:3886`) surfaces every declared NPC on the
Schedule page from day one regardless of any gate, so a schedule given early spoils the entrance.

### The same flag belongs on that character's quest cards

F5 through F8 gate the **canvases**. They say nothing about the **guidance surface**: a Quests page
that lists every character on click one — names, the room each stands in, the hour they are there —
spoils every meeting in the game. The field keeps the name back until the meeting: In Her Own
Hands' [Progress_Hints_Base], behind `<<if not $xr.ab.m>>`, gives only *"I should check out some of
the local shops . . ."*

**A character's `[[quest_cards]]` carry that character's meeting flag in `when`.**

```toml
when = [ { flag = "met_wade", subject = "player", op = "is_true" },
         { trait = "want", subject = "npc", npc_id = "npc_wade", op = "lt", value = 40 } ]
```

The engine already does the rest. `QuestsPage` wraps each character's section in `<<if _card>>`
(`v2.py:17070`) and `setup.pickQuestsCard` returns `null` when no card's `when` matches
(`v2.py:16829`), so an unmet character renders **no heading and no section** — the roster fills in
as the player meets people, which is what the field ships (the-company's cast table is
`<<if $player.met[_char.id]>>` per row).

Three things to get right:

- **A `when` item sets `flag` *or* `trait`, never both** — the importer rejects an item carrying
  both (`template_import.py:5710`). The meeting flag is its own item beside the trait band.
- **Put it on *every* card in that character's ladder**, not just the first. A gap means the
  character reappears at the band whose card you missed.
- **Flag names are not validated against anything.** Nothing checks that `met_wade` exists; a typo
  hides that character's guidance forever and no build error says so. Read the name off the
  meeting canvas's own `flagEffects`, not off memory.

⚠️ **This flag is load-bearing twice.** The cast page (`[ui.cast_page]`, `engine.md` §34) lists a
character exactly when `pickQuestsCard` returns a card for them, so one flag reveals both surfaces
and they cannot fall out of step. The cost is worth stating plainly: **a character with no quest
card can never appear on the cast page.** `guidance exists` already requires every `[[npcs]]` entry
to carry one, so this cannot happen in a game that passes its own scoreboard.

**Story-goal cards — the ones with no `npc_id` — are never gated this way.** They are the
always-live "Story Goals" section, and a guidance page whose every card is gated renders
"No active quests." on turn one.

---

## F9 · A place says what it is on the screen the player keeps coming back to

**The location's own `description` says what kind of place this is and what happens here.** Not a
scene that plays once. The description is the only surface the player sees on *every* visit,
including the twentieth, and "what is this place" is a standing question, not a first-entry one.

**The field names the function on the room screen itself.** Shady Deals' [Pawnshop] renders, on
every visit, *"Pawnshop might buy various electronics and jewelry."* — what the place is, and what
the player does there, in one line.

⚠️ **This is `register.md`'s "words the player has to already own", one level up.** There the unit
was a word; here it is a whole place. A location whose *function* is only implied is an unglossed
noun the size of a room.

### The field's device is the room screen, and it changes

Measured across the 26-game corpus:

```
                                    field median
room prose the player sees per visit   82 words
variant branches per room screen           10
rooms that rotate their text              22%
rooms that vary by hour                   17%
an event renders ON the room screen       yes
```

The place tells its own story every time you walk in, and it is not the same story twice.

### ⚠️ The first-visit canvas is a MINORITY device — do not reach for it first

This section previously taught the opposite, and worked its example from
`degrees-of-lewdity`'s `$forest_shop_intro` / `$gwylan_cafe_intro` family. Counted properly, that
family is **one game**:

```
degrees-of-lewdity   258 first-visit branches, 117 flags     the only game doing it
realm-of-corruption   12
amore · patriarch · sluttown-usa · zaras-school-life · new-life-project     2 each
EIGHTEEN OF TWENTY-SIX GAMES     zero
  — including destroyer, become-someone, course-of-temptation, the-company, friends-of-mine
```

It is a legitimate device and DoL builds a great deal on it. **It is not the default and it does not
substitute for a description that names the function**, because it plays once and the confusion it
is aimed at is permanent. LO ruled on exactly that ground:

> LO: *"I think the place name is description and what was going in that place should be able to
> tell the whole story."*

Reach for a first visit when a place has a **one-time** thing to say — a door that was locked and
now is not, a room whose meaning changes the first time you are let into it. Never as the place's
only introduction.

### Authoring the two halves

**State-variance — `[[locations.description_variants]]`, shipped 2026-08-26.** The base
`description` stays required and becomes the else; each variant is `{conditions, text}` and the
engine emits a first-match chain. Conditions are the ordinary ones, so the most useful axis is
**who is in the room** — which is the "what happens here" half of the rule, told by the room itself:

```toml
[[locations]]
id          = "the_yard"
description = "Gravel from the back step of the house to the roller door of the shop…"

[[locations.description_variants]]
conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [
  { type = "npc_at_location", location_id = "the_shop_floor", operator = "is_present" },
] }
text = "…and the roller door is up. Air tools go in bursts and stop."
```

⚠️ **`version = "1.0"` is not optional.** `triggerConditionsSatisfied` returns **true** for any
`conditions{}` without it, so a variant missing it renders forever and the location's own
description is never seen again. The importer refuses it rather than building green.

⚠️ **There is no time-of-day condition.** The evaluator has `flag`, `trait`, `npc_at_location`,
`stage`, `quest`, `item`, `days_since_flag`, `corruption_level` and the clothing family — and
nothing that reads the hour. So the field's 17%-vary-by-hour column is still **not authorable**;
schedules gate canvases by time, not descriptions. Gate presence-variants on who is there instead,
which is where the hour shows up anyway.

⚠️ **A random ambient still takes the WHOLE screen, and that is an engine limit, not a choice.**
When a Lane 2 ambient rolls on entry the room `<<goto>>`s to it — no title, no description, no
portraits, no exits — so on that visit the description does not render at all. An `ambient_render =
"inline"` setting that gave the ambient the description slot instead was built and **reverted on
2026-08-26**; do not write doctrine or a ledger promise against it. `destroyer` renders its
encounter in the description position and keeps its affordance bar and exits either way, so the
shape is known and the gap is real — it is simply not available today.

### Rotation is still not built

The field's other column — 22% of rooms rotating their text between visits — needs a per-visit
counter like `block_pool`'s and does not exist for descriptions. Do not promise it in a ledger.

---

## F10 · The role stays attached after the introduction

F7 gets the role onto the screen at the meeting. **F9 says a place keeps saying what it is on every
visit. This is the same rule for people, and it is the one that was missing.**

"Who is this" is a **standing** question. A meeting answers it once, and the player then spends forty
visits in a hub where the man is a bare first name.

**Lint `the role stays attached`** (gates.py:5519) takes each character's anchor words from his own
`npcs[].relationship` line and counts how often his own canvases use them, per 10k words. It prints a
list, thinnest first, with no bar. It counts every canvas bound to him, so a re-entered surface and a
one-shot count the same. Reading which is which is yours.

**Where it goes: the surfaces the player RE-ENTERS.** A hub, an ambient, a walk-in. Not the one-shot
that introduced him — that one is already doing its job.

**Both, never one instead of the other.**

> *"Relation and name both are important and both can't be replaced with another. We are not calling
> out for replacing one with another."*

⚠️ **Do not swap the name out for the relation on the speaker line.** `destroyer` does
(`<<speech "teagan" "Stepsister">>`) and it is the only game in the 26-game corpus that does — it
survives it by having **exactly one of each relation**. Relation words on buttons run at **field
median 0.4%, max 2.0%**. `sluttown-usa` is a family premise with 37,408 speaker labels and uses **names only**. Swapping does not remove the memory tax,
it moves it: the player now has to remember who "Stepsister" is.

The cheap form is three words riding in prose that was going to be there anyway: name and relation on
the same line, at the point of use, and the register does not move.

**Put it in a `block_pool` variant rather than in the always-renders text.** A hub pool cycles, so
the anchor recurs periodically instead of arriving every single visit, which is how a reminder turns
into nagging.

### The mechanical half — `npcs[].role`

image                = "locations/linden_street.jpg"
image_search_queries = ["suburban street houses lawns morning", "bus stop suburban corner"]
navigation_order     = ["house"]

image                = "locations/house_hall.jpg"
image_search_queries = ["suburban house front hall staircase", "family home entrance hallway stairs evening"]
entry_from           = "linden_street"
navigation_order     = ["kitchen", "landing", "study"]

entry_from           = "house"

[[locations]]

entry_from           = "landing"

[[locations]]

entry_from           = "landing"

[[locations]]

entry_from           = "landing"

[[locations]]

[[canvases]]
id   = "meet_priya"

[canvases.trigger]
location      = "firm"
requires_npc  = "npc_priya"
is_repeatable = false
priority      = 11
is_active     = true

[[canvases.trigger.schedules]]
weekdays   = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
start_time = "09:00"
end_time   = "17:00"

[canvases.trigger.conditions]
version = "1.0"
logic   = "AND"
items = [
  { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "firm_day1_done", operator = "is_true" },
  { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "met_priya",      operator = "is_false" },
]

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "copy_room"
name = "The copy room"
blocks = [
  { type = "paragraph", content = "A woman in a charcoal suit is waiting at the copy room door with a stack of files on her hip and a pen behind her ear. She's the senior paralegal, mid-thirties, and every intern on this floor answers to her. She looks you over from your heels to your hair, slowly, the way she'd check a contract for mistakes." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "unknown" }, content = "You're the new intern. I'm Priya Shah. Callahan signs your envelope, but I decide what you do all day, and I'm the one who tells him if you're any good." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "office_talk", operator = "gte", value = 3 } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "And I've already heard about you at the coffee machine. That was fast, even for this floor." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "Everyone says you're Martin's. I don't care whose you are. I care if you can file." },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "She drops the stack into your arms. Then she nods past you, at the associate with the loosened tie who has stopped pretending to read his screen." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "Rule one. They'll watch you bend over that copier all day. He already does. You can go red every time, or you can make them wait for their files. The girls who go red don't get kept on." },
  { type = "thought_bubble", props = { speaker = "player" }, content = "She saw all of it. And she's telling me to use it." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "choices"

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "\"Show me where everything goes.\""
targetType = "node"
nodeId     = "meet_priya.tour"

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "\"What if I want them watching?\""
targetType = "node"
nodeId     = "meet_priya.bold"

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "tour"
name = "\"Show me where everything goes.\""
blocks = [
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "Good. Litigation on the left, contracts on the right, and nothing goes on a partner's desk without passing mine first. I'm here from half eight. When you run out of work, you come to me." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "She walks off without checking whether you follow. You follow, and you feel the man with the loose tie watching you do it." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "location"
text = "Get to work."

[canvases.nodes.exit_block.config]
destinationType          = "specific"
locationId               = "firm"
time_progression_minutes = 20
flagEffects = [ { targetType = "player", flag = "met_priya", op = "set" } ]

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "bold"
name = "\"What if I want them watching?\""
blocks = [
  { type = "paragraph", content = "Priya stops. For the first time she looks at you like you might be worth the trouble, and a slow smile pulls at one corner of her mouth." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "Then make it worth their while, and make sure I hear about it before Callahan does. I'm here from half eight. When you run out of work, you come to me." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "She taps the top file against your chest, once, and leaves you holding the stack. Your face is hot, and you're grinning." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "location"
text = "Get to work."

[canvases.nodes.exit_block.config]
destinationType          = "specific"
locationId               = "firm"
time_progression_minutes = 20
flagEffects = [ { targetType = "player", flag = "met_priya", op = "set" } ]
EOF

# Her first shift after day one, inside Priya's own hours (firm, weekdays 08:30–17:30).
# Sets met_priya, which gates hub_priya_copyroom and her quest card.
[[canvases]]
id   = "meet_priya"
name = "The senior paralegal"
description = "Meets Priya, the senior paralegal who trains the interns. Role before name; reads office_talk. Sets met_priya."

[canvases.trigger]
location      = "firm"
requires_npc  = "npc_priya"
is_repeatable = false

is_active     = true

[[canvases.trigger.schedules]]
weekdays   = [0, 1, 2, 3, 4]
start_time = "09:00"
end_time   = "17:00"

[canvases.trigger.conditions]
version = "1.0"
logic   = "AND"
items = [
  { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "firm_day1_done", operator = "is_true" },
  { type = "flag", subject = "player", flag_key = "met_priya",      operator = "is_false" },
]

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "copy_room"
name = "The copy room"
blocks = [
  { type = "paragraph", content = "A woman in a charcoal suit is waiting at the copy room door with a stack of files on her hip and a pen behind her ear. She's the senior paralegal, mid-thirties, and every intern on this floor answers to her. She looks you over from your heels to your hair, slowly, the way she'd check a contract for mistakes." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "unknown" }, content = "You're the new intern. I'm Priya Shah. Callahan signs your envelope, but I decide what you do all day, and I'm the one who tells him if you're any good." },
  { type = "group", props = { conditions = { version = "1.0", logic = "AND", items = [ { type = "trait", subject = "player", trait_key = "office_talk", operator = "gte", value = 3 } ] }, blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "And I've already heard about you at the coffee machine. That was fast, even for this floor." },
  ] } },
  { type = "group", props = { blocks = [
    { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "Everyone says you're Martin's. I don't care whose you are. I care if you can file." },
  ] } },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "She drops the stack into your arms. Then she nods past you, at the associate with the loosened tie who has stopped pretending to read his screen." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "Rule one. They'll watch you bend over that copier all day. He already does. You can go red every time, or you can make them wait for their files. The girls who go red don't get kept on." },
  { type = "thought_bubble", props = { speaker = "player" }, content = "She saw all of it. And she's telling me to use it." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "choices"

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "\"Show me where everything goes.\""
targetType = "node"
nodeId     = "meet_priya.tour"

[[canvases.nodes.exit_block.choices]]
text       = "\"What if I want them watching?\""
targetType = "node"
nodeId     = "meet_priya.bold"

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "tour"
name = "\"Show me where everything goes.\""
blocks = [
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "Good. Litigation on the left, contracts on the right, and nothing goes on a partner's desk without passing mine first. I'm here from half eight. When you run out of work, you come to me." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "She walks off without checking whether you follow. You follow, and you can feel the man with the loose tie watching you do it." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "location"
text = "Get to work."

[canvases.nodes.exit_block.config]
destinationType          = "specific"
locationId               = "firm"
time_progression_minutes = 20
flagEffects = [ { targetType = "player", flag = "met_priya", op = "set" } ]

[[canvases.nodes]]
id   = "bold"
name = "\"What if I want them watching?\""
blocks = [
  { type = "paragraph", content = "Priya stops. For the first time she looks at you like you might be worth the trouble, and a slow smile pulls at one corner of her mouth." },
  { type = "dialog", props = { speaker = "npc", npcId = "npc_priya" }, content = "Then make it worth their while, and make sure I hear about it before Callahan does. I'm here from half eight. When you run out of work, you come to me." },
  { type = "paragraph", content = "She taps the top file against your chest, once, and leaves you holding the stack. Your face is hot, and you're grinning." },
]

[canvases.nodes.exit_block]
type = "location"
text = "Get to work."

destinationType          = "specific"
locationId               = "firm"
